propositions.text: The claimant is a Slovak Republic citizen claiming refugee protection under IRPA ss. 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of the Slovak Republic (Slovakia) and claims refugee protection pursuant to ss. 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).1

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is a Slovak citizen seeking refugee protection under IRPA ss. 96 and 97(1), court states.

propositions.text: The claimant fears persecution by skinheads.
propositions.quote: The claimant fears persecution at the hands of the skinheads.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges fear of persecution by skinheads.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges threats and assaults by persecutors due to Roma ethnicity.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges that he was threatened and assaulted by the agents of persecution on account of his Roma ethnicity.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges threats and assaults due to Roma ethnicity.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The claimant's identity is established by oral testimony and supporting documents.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity is established through his oral testimony and the supporting documentation2 filed.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's identity is established by testimony and documents, court finds.

propositions.text: The claimant filed original PIF in June 2012 and amended narrative in March 2013.
propositions.quote: The claimant filed his original Personal Information Form (PIF) in June 2012 and filed an amendment to his narrative in March 2013.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant filed original PIF in June 2012 and amended narrative in March 2013.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he was attacked in first grade but did not report due to threats.
propositions.quote: In his oral testimony, the claimant stated that while he attended the first grade he was attacked by some of his fellow students. He stated that he did not report this incident to the police because he had been threatened by the assailants if they found out that he had reported them.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified to first grade attack and non-reporting due to threats.

propositions.text: Three months later, claimant assaulted again; parents reported to school authorities and assaults stopped.
propositions.quote: About three months after this assault, the claimant stated that he was assaulted again. This time he and his parents reported the matter to the teacher and the principal and the situation calmed down. He stated that he experienced no other assaults at this school after he had reported the matter to the school authorities.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified second assault reported to school, after which assaults stopped.

propositions.text: In 2005, assaulted by three skinheads; teacher refused to intervene; doctor treated but refused medical report; police refused complaint without medical report.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that in 2005, when he was a high school student, he was assaulted by three skinheads. He reported the incident to the teacher who refused to intervene. Because he had suffered bruises as a result of the incident he attended at a physician's office who gave him a cream for his injuries but refused to give him a medical report. He stated that he tried to file a police report but the police would not accept a denunciation without a report from the doctor.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified 2005 assault by skinheads, no police report due to lack of medical report.

propositions.text: In second year of high school, assaulted again causing head bleeding; doctor treated but refused medical report; police refused complaint without medical report.
propositions.quote: The claimant then stated that while in his second year of high school he was again assaulted by the agents of persecution. As a result of the assault he suffered bleeding from his head. He was taken to a doctor who treated him for his injuries but, once again, refused to give him a medical report. The claimant stated that, as with the previous assault, he was not able to file a denunciation with the authorities because he did not have a medical report.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified second year high school assault with head injury, no medical or police report.

propositions.text: Panel asked claimant why assaults at school were omitted from original PIF narrative.
propositions.quote: The panel pointed out to the claimant that all of these assaults which he alleges he experienced at school had not been mentioned by him in his original PIF narrative and the panel asked him to explain the omission.

propositions.text: Claimant replied he did not know what needed to be included at that time.
propositions.quote: He replied that at that time he did not know what needed to be included.

paragraphs.summary: Panel asked claimant about omissions of school assaults; claimant said he did not know what to include.

propositions.text: Rejects claimant's explanation for omission of school assaults from PIF narrative.
propositions.quote: I reject this explanation.

propositions.text: Omission of assaults is important as it shows early persecution; claimant gave no reasonable explanation.
propositions.quote: The omission is an important fact in the claimant's story for it demonstrates at what early stage in his life he began to experience difficulties at the hands of the agents of persecution.

propositions.text: New oral testimony info amounts to omissions on significant aspects central to claim.
propositions.quote: The new information in his oral testimony amounts to omissions regarding significant aspects that go directly to the heart of the claimant's claim.

propositions.text: On balance of probabilities, claimant was not assaulted during school years by persecutors.
propositions.quote: I find on a balance of probabilities, that the claimant was not assaulted during his school years by the agents of persecution.

propositions.text: Board has been upheld when rejecting major evidence omitted from PIF.
propositions.quote: The Immigration and Refugee Board (Board) has been upheld when rejecting major evidence which has been omitted from the PIF.

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects claimant's explanation for omissions, finds assaults likely did not occur, citing precedent on PIF omissions.

propositions.text: In 2009, claimant was assaulted while shopping; back cut causing kidney problems requiring surgery.
propositions.quote: The claimant then stated that in XXXX of 2009 while shopping, he was again assaulted by the agents of persecution who cut his back. As a result of the injury to his back, the claimant experienced problems with his kidney requiring surgery.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified 2009 assault caused back injury and kidney problems requiring surgery.

propositions.text: Doctor did not provide medical report; police refused complaint without medical report; after surgery police refused report as no indication of persecutors.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that the original doctor who treated him did not provide him with a medical report. Although he tried to file a report with the police, as with other occasions the police refused to take a complaint because he did not have a medical report. The panel asked him if he had returned to the police to file a report after he had undergone his surgery and he replied that he did but because the report did not indicate that the agents of persecution were responsible for the assault the police did not file a report.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified no medical report and police refused complaint; post-surgery police refused report without persecutor indication.

propositions.text: Panel asked claimant why 2009 assault and injuries were omitted from original narrative.
propositions.quote: The panel pointed out to the claimant that this particular incident, including the details of the injuries which he suffered, and the fact that he tried to file a police report, were not mentioned by him in his original narrative and the panel asked him to explain the omission.

propositions.text: Claimant replied he wanted to be concise.
propositions.quote: The claimant replied that he wanted to be concise.

propositions.text: Rejects claimant's explanation; omission is important and central to claim's severity of injuries.
propositions.quote: I reject this explanation. This is not a question of being concise about a fact which the claimant mentioned in his narrative. This is a question of the fact that the claimant failed to make any mention of this particular assault in his narrative. The omission is an important fact in the claimant's story for it demonstrates the severity of the injuries which the claimant suffered as a result of this assault.

propositions.text: New oral testimony info amounts to omissions on significant aspects central to claim.
propositions.quote: The new information in his oral testimony amounts to omissions regarding significant aspects that go directly to the heart of the claimant's claim.

propositions.text: On balance of probabilities, claimant was not assaulted in 2009 by persecutors; Board upheld rejecting major omitted evidence.
propositions.quote: I find on a balance of probabilities, that the claimant was not assaulted in XXXX of 2009 by the agents of persecution. The Board has been upheld when rejecting major evidence which has been omitted from the PIF.

paragraphs.summary: Panel asked about 2009 assault omission; claimant said concise; court rejects, finds assault likely did not occur, citing precedent.

propositions.text: In 2011, claimant attacked by three skinheads; doctor treated but refused medical report; police refused report without medical report.
propositions.quote: The claimant then stated that in XXXX 2011 he was again attacked by three skinheads. As with the other assaults the claimant alleges that he was treated by a doctor after the assault but the doctor refused to provide him with a medical report and because of that the police would not take a report of the assault.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified 2011 assault with doctor treatment but no medical report; police refused report.

propositions.text: Panel asked claimant why 2011 assault was omitted from original narrative.
propositions.quote: The panel pointed out to the claimant that he had not mentioned this assault in his original narrative and he replied that he did not have a clue as to what to include in his original narrative.

propositions.text: Claimant replied he did not know what to include in original narrative.
propositions.quote: he replied that he did not have a clue as to what to include in his original narrative.

propositions.text: Rejects claimant's explanation; original narrative mentions at least one assault; omission is important and central to claim.
propositions.quote: I reject this explanation. The original narrative does make mention of at least one assault. It is reasonable that the claimant would have also remembered this particular assault in his original narrative for it demonstrates the frequency of the assaults which he suffered at the hands of the agents of persecution.

propositions.text: New oral testimony info amounts to omissions on significant aspects central to claim.
propositions.quote: The new information in his oral testimony amounts to omissions regarding significant aspects that go directly to the heart of the claimant's claim.

propositions.text: On balance of probabilities, claimant was not assaulted in 2011 by persecutors; Board upheld rejecting major omitted evidence.
propositions.quote: I find on a balance of probabilities, that the claimant was not assaulted in XXXX 2011 by the agents of persecution. The Board has been upheld when rejecting major evidence which has been omitted from the PIF.

paragraphs.summary: Panel asked about 2011 assault omission; claimant said he did not know what to include; court rejects, finds assault likely did not occur.

propositions.text: In 2012, claimant assaulted by four skinheads causing head bleeding and bruises; doctor refused medical report; police refused report.
propositions.quote: The claimant then stated that in XXXX 2012 he was assaulted by four skinheads. As a result of the injuries he was bleeding in the head and suffered bruises. As with all previous assaults the attending doctor refused to issue a medical report and because of this the claimant could not file a report with the police.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified 2012 assault causing head injuries; no medical report or police report filed.

propositions.text: Panel noted many refugee claims from Slovakia include medical reports from doctors or state institutions.
propositions.quote: The panel pointed out to the claimant that the panel has heard a large number of refugee claims from the Slovak Republic where medical reports from either individual physicians or state health institutions were submitted along with the claims.

propositions.text: Claimant did not believe panel that medical reports had been submitted by Slovak refugee claimants.
propositions.quote: The claimant replied that he did not believe me that medical reports had been submitted to me by refugee claimants from the Slovak Republic.

propositions.text: Panel noted Board documentation does not mention police refusing reports without medical certificates in Slovakia.
propositions.quote: The panel also mentioned to the claimant that the Board's documentation with respect to the Slovak Republic does not mention that the police would not file a report if a medical certificate was not presented.

propositions.text: Panel said if claimant's allegation true, NGOs or international organizations would mention police refusal without medical report.
propositions.quote: The panel pointed out to the claimant that if what he was saying were true, some independent international organization or NGO would make mention of the fact that in the Slovak Republic the police does not issue reports unless they have a medical report of the incident.

propositions.text: Claimant replied that human rights are being violated.
propositions.quote: The claimant replied that human rights are being violated.

paragraphs.summary: Panel noted many Slovak refugee claims have medical reports; claimant denied; panel noted no NGO reports police refusal; claimant said human rights violated.

propositions.text: Rejects claimant's explanation; reasonable to expect international reports to mention police refusal without medical report if true.
propositions.quote: I reject this explanation. It is reasonable to expect that reports of organizations who comment on the difficulties experienced by the Romas in the Slovak Republic would make mention of the fact that, one of the difficulties which they experience, is that the police do not issue a police report if there is no medical report on the assault.

propositions.text: No documentary proof supports claimant's allegation about police refusing reports without medical reports.
propositions.quote: There is no documentary proof to back up the claimant's allegations.

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects claimant's explanation; no documentary proof supports police refusal allegation; expects international reports to mention it if true.

propositions.text: Claimant was not assaulted in XXXX 2012 on a balance of probabilities
propositions.quote: I find, on a balance of probabilities, that the claimant was not assaulted in XXXX 2012.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant was not assaulted in XXXX 2012 on a balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Claimant has not established state protection is unavailable in Slovak Republic
propositions.quote: I find, on a balance of probabilities that the principal claimant has not established that state protection is unavailable for him in the Slovak Republic.

propositions.text: Presumption that state can protect citizens; claimant must rebut with clear and convincing proof of lack of protection
propositions.quote: There is a presumption that a state is capable of protecting its citizens. The claimant may rebut this presumption by providing "clear and convincing" proof of lack of state protection in their country of origin.

propositions.text: Claimant must approach state for protection if reasonably forthcoming
propositions.quote: The claimant must approach his or her state for protection, providing state protection might be reasonably forthcoming.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimant failed to prove lack of state protection; law presumes state protection unless rebutted by clear proof; claimant must seek state protection if reasonable.

propositions.text: Imperfect protection is not clear and convincing proof of state's inability to protect
propositions.quote: Evidence that protection being offered is not necessarily perfect10 is not clear and convincing proof of the state's inability to protect its citizens, as no government can guarantee the protection of all its citizens at all times.

propositions.text: State with effective control and serious efforts to protect citizens is not failing protection despite imperfect success
propositions.quote: where a state is in effective control of its territory, has military, police and civil authority in place, and makes serious efforts to protect its citizens, the mere fact it is not always successful at doing so will not be enough to justify a claim that the victims are unable to avail themselves of protection.

propositions.text: Claimant bears onus to prove state protection inadequate on balance of probabilities
propositions.quote: The onus is on the claimant to establish, on a balance of probabilities, that state protection is inadequate.

paragraphs.summary: Law states imperfect protection is insufficient proof of failure; state with control and efforts is presumed protective; claimant must prove inadequacy on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Burden of proving lack of state protection proportional to state's democracy level
propositions.quote: The burden of proving an absence of state protection is directly proportional to the level of democracy that exists in the state.

propositions.text: Slovak Republic is a functioning democracy with political and judicial systems providing some protection
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence before the Board indicates the Slovak Republic is a functioning democracy. It has functioning political and judicial systems in place and an official apparatus sufficient to provide a measure of protection to its citizens.

propositions.text: Local policing failures do not prove lack of state protection unless part of pattern of state's inability or refusal
propositions.quote: Local failures to provide effective policing do not amount to a lack of state protection unless they are part of a pattern of state's inability or refusal to provide protection.

propositions.text: Claimant must exhaust all reasonable courses of action before concluding state protection unavailable
propositions.quote: Therefore, a claimant must do more than approach one police officer unsuccessfully before deciding that state protection would not be forthcoming. There is an onus on the claimant to exhaust all courses of action reasonably available to him.

paragraphs.summary: Law requires burden proportional to democracy; court finds Slovak Republic democratic with protection; local failures not enough; claimant must exhaust reasonable options.

propositions.text: Slovak Republic controls territory with functioning security forces and no total breakdown of authority
propositions.quote: The Slovak Republic is in control of its territory and has functioning security forces, both military and police, in place. There is no evidence of a total breakdown of state authority in the country.

propositions.text: Heavy burden to show one should not exhaust all domestic recourse avenues
propositions.quote: Therefore, the burden of attempting to show that one should not be required to exhaust all avenues of domestic recourse is a heavy one.

propositions.text: Slovak security forces are hierarchical and allow complaints to higher authority if dissatisfied
propositions.quote: The Slovak Republic security forces are hierarchical and allow a person to complain to a higher authority, particularly the Bureau for the Inspection Service of the Police Corps, if dissatisfied with the services provided.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Slovak Republic controls territory with functioning security forces; heavy burden to avoid exhausting domestic remedies; complaints can be escalated.

propositions.text: Credibility finding made on all alleged assaults suffered by claimant
propositions.quote: In this particular claim, I have made a credibility finding with respect to all of the alleged assaults suffered by the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: Court made credibility finding on all alleged assaults suffered by claimant.

propositions.text: There is state protection for Roma community members in Slovak Republic
propositions.quote: I find that there is state protection for members of the Roma community in the Slovak Republic.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds state protection exists for Roma community members in Slovak Republic.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows Roma and minorities face discrimination and violence in Slovak Republic
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence of the Board19 and counsel's documents20 do indicate that Roma and other minorities suffer discrimination and violence in the Slovak Republic and that police mistreat Romani suspects and detainees.

propositions.text: Organized neo-Nazi groups harass and attack Roma and minorities; police may not always intervene properly
propositions.quote: The evidence also supports the claimant's contention that organized neo-Nazi groups and sympathizers harass and attack minorities including the Roma. Further, police might not intervene or investigate properly when there are Roma involved, although this varies by jurisdiction.

propositions.text: Roma face discrimination in healthcare, education, housing, and employment in Slovak Republic
propositions.quote: The Roma generally face discrimination in health care, education, housing and employment in the Slovak Republic as well.

propositions.text: Many Roma face severe difficulties accessing adequate housing, employment, and experience segregation in schools and healthcare
propositions.quote: Many Roma face severe difficulties and discrimination accessing adequate housing and employment and they experience segregation in schools and health care facilities.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds evidence that Roma face discrimination, violence, police mistreatment, and segregation in Slovak Republic.

propositions.text: Slovak Republic has taken steps and shows progress combating deficiencies affecting Roma
propositions.quote: However, the documentary evidence indicates that the Slovak Republic has taken, and is taking, steps to combat these deficiencies and there are signs of real progress.

propositions.text: Slovak legal framework includes Constitution, legislation, and international obligations to combat these problems
propositions.quote: For example, there is a deeply entrenched legal framework as a basis from which the Slovak Republic can combat these problems. The legal framework includes the Constitution, legislation and international obligations as well.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Slovak Republic has legal framework and is making progress combating Roma-related deficiencies.

propositions.text: Government took proactive steps addressing discrimination and violence against minorities, including Roma
propositions.quote: I note that the government has taken proactive steps to address the issues of discrimination and violence targeting minorities, in particular the Roma.

propositions.text: 2009 police incident in Košice involving mistreatment of Romani boys and subsequent dismissals and pending court case
propositions.quote: Sources provide the 2009 example in which police officers in Košice detained six Romani boys, forced them to strip, hit and kiss each other, threatened them with loaded guns, unleashed police dogs on them, and yelled anti-Roma statements at them (ERRC Mar. 2011, 28; Council of Europe Feb. 2012, 77). Six police officers and four senior officials were reportedly dismissed following the incident (ibid.). The ERRC states that three officers were still employed by the police force at the time of the first court hearing on 26 August 2010 (Mar. 2011, 28). The court case against the police officers involved in the incident was reportedly pending at the end of 2011 (AI 2012; US 24 May 2012, 2).

propositions.text: National Roma Integration Strategy 2012 adopted focusing on education, employment, healthcare, housing
propositions.quote: The National Roma Integration Strategy up to 2020 was adopted by the government in January 2012, in accordance with its obligations as a member of the EU, and focuses on four main areas: education, employment, healthcare, and housing (UN 24 May 2012).

propositions.text: Strategy goals include halting segregation, fostering inclusion, non-discrimination, and changing majority attitudes
propositions.quote: According to the government, the goals of the strategy are "to halt the segregation of Roma communities; to facilitate a significant positive turn in the social inclusion of Roma communities; to foster non-discrimination; and to change the attitude of the majority population toward the Roma minority" (Slovak Republic [2011]).

propositions.text: Roma communities consulted in strategy development; strategy has concrete measures, financial commitments, and monitoring
propositions.quote: Sources indicate that Roma communities were consulted throughout the development process of the strategy (OSF 14 June 2012; UN 24 May 2012). According to the OSF representative, the integration strategy is a "great" policy with "concrete measures, financial commitments, and time frames" (14 June 2012). According to the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the strategy includes a regular monitoring mechanism (UN 24 May 2012).

propositions.text: Slovak Republic submits progress reports as member of Decade of Roma Inclusion 2005-2015
propositions.quote: In correspondence with the Research Directorate, an official at the Embassy of the Slovak Republic in Ottawa indicated that as a member of the Decade of Roma Inclusion 2005-2015, the Slovak Republic regularly submits progress reports (Slovak Republic 13 June 2012).

paragraphs.summary: Court notes government took proactive steps including 2009 police incident response and 2012 Roma Integration Strategy with consultation and monitoring.

propositions.text: Slovakia's 2004 Anti-Discrimination Act prohibits discrimination in various fields but is under-implemented
propositions.quote: Slovakia's Anti-Discrimination Act (Act), which was adopted in 2004, prohibits direct and indirect discrimination on the grounds of race, nationality, ethnic origin, among others, in the fields of education, social security, employment, healthcare, and access to goods and services. According to the Council of Europe, the Act is "largely under-implemented" due to inadequate awareness of discrimination of the Act among the legal profession, lengthy court proceedings, and a "reported reluctance to [grant] meaningful compensation."

paragraphs.summary: Document shows Slovakia's 2004 Anti-Discrimination Act prohibits discrimination but is under-implemented due to awareness and legal issues.

propositions.text: Authorities have taken many measures to mitigate Roma discrimination including funding education, healthcare, employment, and living conditions
propositions.quote: The objective evidence makes clear that the authorities in Slovakia have taken a plethora of measures to mitigate the discrimination faced by the Roma. The government has funded education, health care, employment and improved living conditions for the Roma.

propositions.text: Slovakia prioritizes social inclusion of marginalized Roma communities through programs and policies
propositions.quote: Slovakia pays appropriate attention to the social inclusion of Roma. Support of social inclusion of persons endangered by social exclusion or socially excluded persons through the development of services with special focus on marginalized Roma communities is among priorities of the Operational Programme Employment and Social Inclusion (2007-2013).

propositions.text: Despite efforts, Roma remain underemployed and less educated; government sets objectives to improve labor market access and education
propositions.quote: Despite these efforts by the Slovak Republic government, statistics indicate that Roma are still underemployed and less educated. The government has set objectives focused on the improvement of access to work opportunities with particular emphasis on non-discriminatory access to the labour market as well as on active policies and programmes directed to the labour market, education, continuing education, and the support of self-employment activities.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds authorities have taken many measures to mitigate Roma discrimination but Roma remain underemployed and less educated.

propositions.text: Information on Roma in Slovakia is mixed with problems including anti-Roma governor election and extremist violence
propositions.quote: I note that the information is mixed as it relates to the Roma in Slovakia, there are problems in certain areas including in the election of an anti-Roma governor, the violence by extremists and other violent entities that specifically target Romas and other minorities.

propositions.text: Overall evidence shows concrete police action to protect Roma and minorities
propositions.quote: Overall I find there is evidence of a concrete action taken on the part of the police to offer protection to the Roma and other minorities.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds mixed information on Roma issues but overall police take concrete action to protect Roma and minorities.

propositions.text: State does not condone or acquiesce in racial and discriminatory behavior by extremists or skinheads
propositions.quote: Despite the negative reporting, the documentary evidence reveals that the state does not condone or acquiesce in the racial and discriminatory behaviour, particularly at the hands of extremists and/or skinheads.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds state does not condone racial or discriminatory behavior by extremists or skinheads.

propositions.text: Concerns exist about impunity and insufficient police response to racially motivated attacks
propositions.quote: There are legitimate concerns from some groups that there is impunity for racially motivated attacks and the police responses are not sufficient;

propositions.text: Preponderance of evidence shows state takes action against extremists and does not condone extremist actions
propositions.quote: the preponderance of evidence indicates that the state is taking action against extremists and does not condone or assent to extremist actions.

propositions.text: State takes operational action to address discrimination and violence targeting Roma
propositions.quote: I note there is also some evidence that at the operational level the state is taking action to address the discrimination and violence targeting the Roma population.

propositions.text: Despite efforts, Roma remain underemployed and less educated; critics say programs insufficient but evidence shows improvements
propositions.quote: Despite these efforts by the Slovak government, statistics indicate that Roma are still underemployed and less educated. Critics claim these programs do not go far enough or are just superficial. Even so, I find the preponderance of evidence is that there are programs in place resulting in improvements to the lives of Roma.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds concerns about impunity but evidence shows state acts against extremists and discrimination; Roma still face challenges but programs improve lives.

propositions.text: Slovak Republic has undertaken significant efforts to provide better protection and combat corruption
propositions.quote: The above-noted examples indicate that, on the whole, the Slovak Republic has undertaken significant efforts to provide better protection for its citizens and is making serious effort to combat corruption.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Slovak Republic has made significant efforts to improve protection and combat corruption.

propositions.text: Citizens have right to complain about unlawful police conduct; Ministry's Control and Inspection Services investigate complaints
propositions.quote: Documentary evidence states that citizens have the right to lodge complaints against the unlawful conduct of police officers. European Partners Against Corruption (EPAC), a network of European national police oversight bodies and anti-corruption authorities indicates that the Section of Control and Inspection Services (of the Ministry of the Interior) has investigative, supervisory and inspection tasks related to disciplinary matters, criminal matters and service regulation.

propositions.text: Control and Inspection Services is independent from police management but some question its independence
propositions.quote: The Ministry of the Interior states that the section of Control and Inspection Services is a "separate unit" of the Ministry which is "independent from the management and structures of the police" and subordinated to the Ministry of the Interior. However, several sources question the degree of independence of the section.

propositions.text: Complaints investigated by police investigator; Ombudsman's office can review police procedure cases
propositions.quote: Complaints are investigated by a police force investigator. A representative of the Slovak Republic's Office of the Public Defender of Rights, or the ombudsman's office, indicated that their office does have the jurisdiction to review cases related to police procedures or inactivity.

propositions.text: In 2010, authorities charged 122 police officers with 167 crimes including abuse of power, corruption, and assault
propositions.quote: According to the United States Department of State, Country Reports 2011, authorities charged 122 police officers with 167 crimes in 2010. Disciplinary actions ranged from fines to removing officers from the police force. There were 47 cases of "abuse of power," 11 cases of corruption and seven cases of obstruction of justice. Other charges reportedly included battery, assault and battery and illegal intrusion into homes.

paragraphs.summary: Evidence shows citizens can complain about police; Control and Inspection Services investigate but independence questioned; many police charged with crimes in 2010.

propositions.text: Police service varies by jurisdiction; police response to racially motivated crimes has improved but challenges remain
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence indicates that police service may vary depending on the jurisdiction but the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe (COE) reported that police response to racially motivated crimes has improved although it continues to face challenges.

propositions.text: Slovak Republic established Commission to coordinate actions against racially motivated crime and discrimination
propositions.quote: The COE credits this improvement to the Slovak Republic's establishment of a Commission for Co-ordinating Actions to Eliminate Racially Motivated Crime, which is tasked with sharing information on racially motivated crime and eliminating racial discrimination, including police mistreatment.

propositions.text: Slovak Republic has 231 Police Roma specialists spending 70% time in Roma communities to build trust
propositions.quote: The Slovak Republic has implemented an outreach initiative consisting of 231 "Police Roma specialists" who spend 70 percent of their time in Roma communities to build trust.

propositions.text: 120 police officers trained on policing in multiethnic environment; government committed to recruiting Roma officers
propositions.quote: The Commissioner of Human Rights stated that 120 police officers have been trained on "policing in a multiethnic environment," particularly Roma areas, and noted that the government has committed to recruiting Roma police officers to the national police force and to the municipal police.

paragraphs.summary: Evidence shows police response to racially motivated crimes improved; Commission and Police Roma specialists established; training and recruitment efforts ongoing.

propositions.text: Police take action and prosecute racially motivated attacks; several detained in 2011; special police unit monitors extremist activities
propositions.quote: Police do take action when they are requested to do so and that state does prosecute. Investigation of racially motivated attacks against Roma in 2011 varied by jurisdiction, but also states that several people were detained for racially motivated attacks. The Slovak Republic government is reportedly implementing a plan that includes a special police unit in charge of monitoring extremist activities.

propositions.text: Some police officers biased against Roma, especially in Eastern Slovakia and rural areas; complaints may be ignored or inadequately handled
propositions.quote: There is documentary evidence that indicates that some police officers are biased against Roma, particularly in Eastern Slovakia and in rural areas and they may ignore complaints or fail to adequately deal with incidents against Roma.

propositions.text: Few perpetrators prosecuted or imprisoned for violence against Roma
propositions.quote: Further, only a limited number of perpetrators are successfully prosecuted in cases of violence against Roma, and even fewer receive prison sentences.

paragraphs.summary: Evidence shows police prosecute racially motivated attacks and monitor extremists but some officers biased and few perpetrators prosecuted or imprisoned.

propositions.text: Slovak Republic has 231 Police Roma specialists spending 70% time in Roma communities to build trust
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence indicates the Slovak Republic has implemented an outreach initiative consisting of 231 "Police Roma specialists" who spend 70 percent of their time in Roma communities to build trust.

propositions.text: 120 police officers trained on policing in multiethnic environment; government committed to recruiting Roma officers
propositions.quote: The Commissioner of Human Rights stated that 120 police officers have been trained on "policing in a multiethnic environment," particularly Roma areas, and noted that the government has committed to recruiting Roma police officers to the national police force and to the municipal police.

paragraphs.summary: Evidence shows Slovak Republic has Police Roma specialists and trained officers; government committed to recruiting Roma police officers.

propositions.text: Employees can protect rights against discrimination through representatives, labour inspectorates, or courts.
propositions.quote: employees may protect their rights not only with their employer, but also through the intermediary of employee representatives, labour inspectorates, or the court if they consider themselves affected by failure to apply the principle of equal treatment.

propositions.text: Employees may demand cessation of discrimination and rectification or satisfaction.
propositions.quote: They may further demand that the entity that failed to apply the principle of equal treatment refrains from such conduct and, where possible, rectifies the unlawful situation or provides adequate satisfaction.

propositions.text: Applicants can seek pecuniary compensation for employer discrimination in access to employment by court claim.
propositions.quote: In cases where the employer violates the principle of equal treatment with regard to access to employment, the applicant has the right to seek adequate pecuniary compensation by filing a claim with the court.

propositions.text: Right to education in a national minority language is constitutionally protected.
propositions.quote: With respect to education, right to education in a national minority language is enshrined in the Constitution.

propositions.text: A national project aimed to improve Roma education and employment by addressing language, cultural, mobility, and socioeconomic barriers.
propositions.quote: The national project on "Improving the qualification potential of the Roma community by introducing a new course on Roma studies in the system of secondary schools" was carried out under the professional guidance of the National Institute for Education was aimed at eliminating the limited access of the Roma to education and employment due to the language barrier, cultural handicaps, low mobility, and social and economic situation of families and raising educational attainment of the Roma in the Slovak Republic as a basic prerequisite for their participation in the labour market and integration into society in general.

paragraphs.summary: The court states employees can protect against discrimination through various means, and a national project aims to improve Roma education and employment.

propositions.text: Constitution guarantees national minorities the right to create and maintain educational institutions.
propositions.quote: the Constitution guarantees the right of the citizens belonging to national minorities to create and maintain their educational institutions.

propositions.text: Languages of national minorities are taught in state-run higher education institutions funded by the state.
propositions.quote: The teaching of the languages of national minorities is provided also in state-run institutions of higher education. These schools are part of the Slovak Republic's system of education and instruction and are financed from the state budget.

propositions.text: Education for socially disadvantaged children uses specific methods to meet their needs under the Act.
propositions.quote: Education and instruction of children and pupils from socially disadvantaged environment is carried out in schools under this Act using specific methods and forms to meet the needs of these disadvantaged students.

propositions.text: Compulsory education is employed for all students by the state.
propositions.quote: The state employs compulsory education for all students.

propositions.text: Subsidies exist for food, school materials, and motivational allowances for children in low-income families.
propositions.quote: There are subsidies on food, school materials and subsidy on motivational allowance for children attending preschool facilities or schools and living in families that receive benefits and allowances or whose income does not exceed the level of subsistence minimum.

propositions.text: School attendance improved but educational attainment of disadvantaged pupils has not improved.
propositions.quote: Under these programs school attendance of pupils has improved but educational attainment of pupils from socially disadvantaged environment has not improved.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes constitutional rights for minority education, state subsidies, and notes improved attendance but not educational attainment for disadvantaged pupils.

propositions.text: Roma still face higher unemployment and lower educational achievement, and exclusion from housing and health care.
propositions.quote: The evidence clearly shows that the Roma still suffer from higher rates of unemployment and lower educational achievement. The Roma are still excluded from regular life in terms of housing and health care.

propositions.text: State is making serious efforts to combat racial discrimination, with signs of progress despite setbacks.
propositions.quote: the documentary evidence indicates that the state is making serious efforts and although progress is slow, there are signs of progress.

propositions.text: It is unreasonable to expect state measures to have eliminated all racism or violence.
propositions.quote: It is unreasonable to expect that these measures should have prevented or eliminated all racism or acts of violence related to race.

propositions.text: State commitment to combat racial discrimination is not in question despite slow progress and obstacles.
propositions.quote: the commitment of the state to continue the battle is not in question.

propositions.text: Roma existence is not threatened by the state, which acts against extremists threatening Roma.
propositions.quote: their existence is not threatened by the state. While skinheads and extremists seek to threaten the existence of the Roma, the state takes serious actions against that as well.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Roma face disadvantages but the state is committed and acting against racial discrimination and threats.

propositions.text: Bribery and corruption remain issues in Slovak security forces.
propositions.quote: There is information in the documentation to indicate that bribery and corruption remain issues in Slovakian security forces.

propositions.text: Slovak Republic acknowledges past problems and is making serious efforts to rectify corruption and impunity.
propositions.quote: the Slovak Republic candidly acknowledges its past problems and is making serious efforts to rectify the corruption and impunity that exists.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes ongoing corruption issues but acknowledges Slovak Republic's serious efforts to address them.

propositions.text: There is adequate state protection in Slovakia for crime victims; police are willing and able to protect victims.
propositions.quote: there is adequate state protection in the Slovak Republic for victims of crime, that the Slovak Republic is making serious efforts to address the problems of criminality, and that the police are both willing and able to protect victims.

propositions.text: Police corruption and deficiencies exist but are not systemic and are being addressed.
propositions.quote: Police corruption and deficiencies, although existing and noted by the Board, are not systemic. I am of the view in canvassing the documentary evidence, that, as a whole, the issues of corruption and deficiencies are being addressed by the Slovak Republic.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds adequate state protection for crime victims and that police corruption is not systemic and is being addressed.

propositions.text: Corruption in Slovak police and judiciary is ongoing, including police corruption at the border affecting human smuggling efforts.
propositions.quote: corruption in the Slovak police and judiciary system is an ongoing problem as there were reports of corruption and misconduct in the police forces. For instance, police corruption at the border "may have hampered" efforts to reduce human smuggling.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes ongoing corruption in police and judiciary, including border police corruption affecting anti-smuggling efforts.

propositions.text: In 2005, Transparency International ranked Slovakia 47th out of 158 countries, showing significant improvement from previous year.
propositions.quote: For the year 2005, Transparency International (TI) puts Slovakia at the 47th rank out of 158 evaluated countries ranked from the least to the most corrupt. TI stated that Slovakia was among the countries to improve the most in comparison with the previous year.

paragraphs.summary: The court reports Slovakia's 2005 Transparency International ranking as 47th with notable improvement.

propositions.text: Judicial reforms began in 1999 increasing state action against corruption; 90% of anti-corruption plan implemented by 2004.
propositions.quote: In 1999, a program of judicial reforms that increased state action against corruption began. According to Country Reports 2004, 90 per cent of the Slovak Republic's "Government Action Plan to Fight Corruption" was implemented at year's end.

propositions.text: EU summary stated Slovakia must continue efforts to implement national anti-corruption program.
propositions.quote: a European Union (EU) summary of legislation stated that "Slovakia must pursue its efforts to implement its national programme of action."

paragraphs.summary: The court notes judicial reforms since 1999 with 90% anti-corruption plan implementation, but EU urges continued efforts.

propositions.text: US report in 2005 acknowledged legislative strides against corruption but noted challenges in executing new measures.
propositions.quote: United States' International Narcotics Control Strategy Report 2005 reported that, "Slovakia has made major legislative strides in the fight against corruption" it also indicated that the execution of the new measures "remain[ed] a challenge."

paragraphs.summary: The court cites a US report acknowledging legislative progress but challenges in implementing anti-corruption measures.

propositions.text: Slovak government created Anti-Corruption Department in 2002 to apply national anti-corruption program and propose laws.
propositions.quote: The Slovak government created its "Anti-Corruption Department" in December 2002 and put it in charge of applying its national anti-corruption program. This department develops policy, concepts and programs, and proposes laws on combating corruption.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Slovakia created an Anti-Corruption Department in 2002 to lead anti-corruption efforts and law proposals.

propositions.text: Recent state measures include key officials, conflict of interest law, special prosecutor and court, whistleblower statute, and sting operations.
propositions.quote: Officials serious about creating transparent rules and prosecuting abuses have been put in key positions, a new conflict of interest law passed in 2004, and a special prosecutor and court to fight corruption were set up. The head of the [Government of Slovakia] anticorruption office is a noted human rights lawyer who encourages the use of "sting" operations and introduced a "whistle blower" statute to protect government employees who talk to investigators about corruption in their offices.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes recent Slovak anti-corruption measures including new laws, special prosecutor, and whistleblower protections.

propositions.text: Special court and prosecutor for corruption crimes started work in Bratislava by November 2005 with exclusive jurisdiction.
propositions.quote: the Special Court and prosecutor had started their work and that they had "exclusive jurisdiction over domestic and foreign bribery."

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the special anti-corruption court and prosecutor began work in Bratislava by late 2005.

propositions.text: Justice minister acknowledged low confidence in judiciary but random case assignment improved transparency.
propositions.quote: The justice minister of Slovakia recognized that confidence in the Slovak justice system was "low." He stated, however, that a reform through which judges are assigned cases randomly had helped to "improv[e] transparency in the judicial system."

propositions.text: Computerized case assignment system implemented at almost all court levels.
propositions.quote: Country Reports 2004 added that the computerized system assigning cases was implemented at almost all court levels.

paragraphs.summary: The court reports judiciary reforms including random case assignments and computerized systems improving transparency.

propositions.text: Program permits plea bargaining with informants and legalizes undercover agents to fight corruption.
propositions.quote: a program which permits plea bargaining with people who have inside information about organized crime and "the legalization of the use of undercover agents" in the fight against corruption was also put forward.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes a program allowing plea bargaining and undercover agents to combat corruption.

propositions.text: Laws amended to apply zero tolerance to corruption and criminalize failure to disclose corruption; freedom of information law increased transparency.
propositions.quote: Laws regulating professional codes of conduct were amended to make sure that the principle of "zero tolerance" would be applied in cases of corruption. Another legislative change, criminalizing "failure to disclose corruption," was implemented in December 2003. Freedom House added that the Law on Free Access to Information increased transparency.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes legislative changes enforcing zero tolerance on corruption and increasing transparency.

propositions.text: In May 2004, special prosecutor charged Bratislava-Raca mayor with bribery and referred other cases to anticorruption court.
propositions.quote: In May 2004, the appointed "special prosecutor to fight corruption" brought charges against the mayor of Bratislava-Raca, who was suspected of accepting a bribe, and referred other cases to an anticorruption court.

paragraphs.summary: The court reports the special prosecutor charged a mayor with bribery and referred other cases to the anticorruption court in 2004.

propositions.text: In 2004, alien detention facility director arrested for human smuggling; corruption charges pressed against customs and immigration police.
propositions.quote: Over the year 2004, the director of the "alien detention facility" was arrested as a suspect in human smuggling and "several corruption charges" were pressed against members of the customs and immigration police.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes arrests and corruption charges against officials in 2004 related to human smuggling and police corruption.

propositions.text: Claimant has not established that state protection would be unavailable or unreasonable to seek upon return to Slovakia.
propositions.quote: The claimant has not established that were he to return to the Slovak Republic today, state protection would not be reasonably forthcoming or that it is objectively unreasonable for him to seek that protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant failed to prove state protection would be unavailable or unreasonable to seek in Slovakia.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to prove inadequate state protection on balance of probabilities and failed to rebut presumption of protection with clear evidence.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant has not established, on a balance of probabilities, there is inadequate state protection for him in the Slovak Republic. I find the claimant has failed to rebut the presumption of state protection with clear and convincing evidence and his claim fails under sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed to prove inadequate state protection and his claim fails under IRPA sections 96 and 97.

propositions.text: Claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I therefore determine that claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection.

propositions.text: The Refugee Protection Division rejects his claim.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division therefore rejects his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The Refugee Protection Division rejects his claim, the court states.
